seo.title: Business Report
seo.description: Kura business report: what was built, operating data as of 30 October 2026, the business model, the timeline, and why it stopped.

report.title: Business Report
report.subtitle: What Kura built, how it performed, and why it stopped. Kura Finance LLC has been dissolved and has ceased operations.

summary.title: Summary
summary.lede: Kura was a consumer fintech app built around one idea: you keep custody of your money and your data.
summary.prose: A single account let users hold stablecoins in a self-custody smart wallet, move money in and out of bank accounts in five regions, buy tokenized US stocks, earn DeFi yield, and see their net worth across banks, brokers, exchanges, and wallets. The server could not decrypt that financial data.

items.title: Too broad, too early.
items.text: Wallet, card, stocks, DeFi, aggregation, and business treasuries all shipped before a single wedge found product-market fit. The card alone went through three partner approaches without launching.

items.title: The ramp margin could not absorb returns.
items.text: Ramp fees earned 381.32 USDC on about US$34K of gross deposits, but about 54% of that money was sent back, and the wire-return fees on those refunds wiped out all fiat-ramp revenue. The cost could not be passed on: fees are only collected when a deposit converts, converted funds land in the user’s own wallet where they cannot be clawed back, and every workaround either made successful deposits subsidize failed ones, cut off the core user base, or broke the non-custodial promise.

items.title: Regulated money movement is an operations business.
items.text: KYC rejections (64 of 249), fraud-rate thresholds, recalls, refunds, and per-account fees demand dedicated compliance capacity that a solo founder cannot sustain next to engineering.

items.title: Activation is the real funnel.
items.text: 249 KYC starts led to 68 approvals and 18 funded accounts. Onboarding friction, not features, was the constraint.

items.title: The users were not the ones the product was designed for.
items.text: Kura was built for US-style multi-asset users, but 81% of users came from Southeast Asia, Latin America, and Africa, looking for USD and EUR receiving accounts. Only 2 were in the US. Cross-border wires into those accounts are the likely cause of the high refund rate.

items.title: Subscriptions were never validated.
items.text: No one paid for Pro or Ultimate; the three Pro subscriptions were all invoiced at $0.

items.title: What worked.
items.text: Shipping speed (519 production deploys), a security architecture that holds up to scrutiny, and a clean, documented codebase that others can fork.
